evidence: app/models/blocked_email.rb:12 uses BlockedEmail.where(email: email) - a plain case-sensitive `=` on a varchar column (db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:4, no citext/lower index). app/models/user.rb:87 (new_from_params) assigns params[:email] unnormalized, and lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13 passes the raw value. So a block on user@example.com is bypassed by User@Example.com or user@EXAMPLE.com.

lib/email.rb:21 does email.gsub(/^(.+@{1})([^@]+)$/) { $1 + $2.downcase }, so only the domain is lowercased and the local part is left alone. Using Email.downcase would still let USER@example.com bypass a block on user@example.com. A full downcase (or lower(email) in the query) is needed to close the bypass.

app/models/blocked_email.rb:3 only has before_validation :set_defaults, which sets action_type only. Admin-entered emails are stored as typed, and the uniqueness validation (line 5) plus the unique index are case-sensitive, so mixed-case rows never match lowercase lookups and near-duplicates are allowed. Downcasing on save is the other half of the fix for ids 0 and 3.

app/models/blocked_email.rb:12 queries the raw input. Querying with email.downcase (with stored values also normalized, id 2) makes matching case-insensitive. This is the same underlying defect as id 0.

lib/validators/email_validator.rb:19-21 builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) with no end anchor, so 'user@example.com.evil.com' =~ /@(example\.com)/i matches. That bypasses the whitelist (line 5) and blacklists unrelated domains such as example.community. The same logic was in the removed User#email_in_restriction_setting?, so the bug predates this PR, but the PR moves it into a new validator it now owns.

lib/validators/email_validator.rb:20: with @(?:#{domains})\z the pipe-separated domain list stays grouped and must end the string, which fixes the suffix bypass from id 4. The case-insensitive flag stays. The capture group isn't used anywhere (line 21 only tests truthiness), so a non-capturing group is fine.

spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb:4,22 have blank lines inside the describe block. The repo has no .rubocop.yml, and the sibling spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:4,47 and app/models/blocked_email.rb:2,24 use the same padding, so this matches the codebase's style and no linter enforces anything else.

The server side already uses user.email.blocked (lib/validators/email_validator.rb:14; config/locales/server.en.yml:734). The client code at create_account_controller.js (rejectedEmails branch, ~line 69) shows user.email.invalid, which reads 'Please enter a valid email address.' (client.en.yml:216). That message is misleading for a blocked, not-allowed or already-taken email. However, user.email.blocked exists only in server.en.yml, not client.en.yml, so switching the client key would show a missing-translation string. Also, rejectedEmails collects every server email error, not only blocks (create_account_controller.js ~line 274). The better fix is to show the server's result.errors.email message or add a generic client key.

Once an email is in rejectedEmails, emailValidation fails (create_account_controller.js ~lines 69-74) and submitDisabled returns true (line 21), so the same email can't be submitted again. Even if a duplicate were pushed, the array is only used for .contains() membership checks, which duplicates don't affect.
